blockers.quote: The narrator says it once: whenever you share good news, or say what you're going for, a paper meter from plus one hundred to minus one hundred opens above everyone who hears, each time you say it, for sixty seconds, then shuts.
blockers.why: Check #16 fails: the rule, meaning, ambiguity and flagged limit require more than three spoken lines.
blockers.fix: Use three lines: “Say good news—or what you're going for—out loud to a face, and for sixty seconds a meter opens from plus one hundred to minus one hundred.” / “Plus one hundred: pure joy for you. Minus one hundred: they want you to fail.” / “It never says why; calls, texts and posts open nothing. Remember that.”

blockers.quote: Exam day: last year the country grounded flights for thirty-five minutes during the English listening test (c02), a paper plane held still over the halls; about a hundred and forty flights rescheduled, the stock market an hour late, police motorbikes rushing late students to the gates (c02).
blockers.why: Check #7 fails: thirty-five minutes, one hundred and forty flights and an hour arrive together instead of one number breaking the belief.
blockers.fix: Replace with: “For thirty-five minutes, no plane crosses the sky while you listen (c02).” Show the market and police visually without narrating their numbers.

suggestions.quote: You stand on the academy steps and say it into the crowd.
suggestions.fix: Make this a deliberate consequence of Tae-ho's minus six: you announce from the steps to test whether distance from your lane makes the numbers fade.
Replace the named feeling with the picture: “Your score reaches the top. Min-jun's chair beside you stays empty.”

suggestions.quote: At the 1992 Olympics, bronze medallists looked happier than silver: silver thinks of the gold it nearly won, bronze of nearly winning nothing (c08). Across eleven studies, the most common regret of a life is education, about a third of all regrets (c11).
suggestions.fix: Cut the bronze comparison and move the education-regret fact onto the bus ride; let the letter and brushes carry the dock revelation without a two-fact explanation after the peak.

keep.quote: A tag has one colour for every kind of hurt.
A text would open nothing. You could keep her forever on a screen.
You said nobody outside your lane bleeds. She was never outside your lane. She was in it first.
